subject: feat/reply-metadata: optional replyTo engagement metadata (protocol + both adapters + gateway turn header)

environment.notes: No node_modules and no discord.js in this checkout; `bun install` was prohibited. The three modules under test are dependency-free (protocol imports are `import type`, erased at runtime), so they are exercised directly. Files importing discord.js/@gajaeway/sdk cannot be imported here and are asserted against their source text instead.

commands.command: bun test packages/protocol packages/adapter-discord packages/adapter-telegram packages/gateway
commands.comparison: identical failure and error counts as the same command on the base commit; every failure is a pre-existing missing-module or unix-socket failure in files this change does not touch
identical failure and error counts as the same command on the base commit; +95 passing tests

contractCoverage.obligation: replyTo is optional and additive: a non-reply produces no replyTo key and a byte-identical turn header
cases: resolveReplyContext({}) and ({reference:null}) are undefined
resolveTelegramReplyContext(undefined) is undefined
composeTurnHeader for a non-reply is exactly `[<speaker> | <place> (author:<id>, msg:<id>)]`
the author:? placeholder path is identical for engagement undefined and {}
an empty replyTo object leaks no reply clause

contractCoverage.obligation: Discord reply metadata from message.reference + mentions.repliedUser, no network fetch, partial data reported not dropped, forwards are not replies
cases: reference without a usable messageId is not a reply (null, empty, whitespace, absent)
reference.type 1 (forward) and other non-default types are not replies
missing repliedUser still reports the messageId
blank username and blank globalName yield an id with no authorName
globalName precedes username; blank globalName falls through

contractCoverage.obligation: Telegram reply metadata from reply_to_message; message_thread_id/is_topic_message is never a reply
cases: a forum-topic message with is_topic_message and message_thread_id but no reply_to_message yields no reply metadata
message_id 0 keeps the relationship (falsy but valid id)
anonymous channel post keeps the id and leaves author fields absent
string and numeric ids normalise identically

contractCoverage.obligation: fromSelf derives from the same bot identity as mention detection and is absent, not false, when the referenced author is unknown
cases: empty botId with a resolved author leaves fromSelf absent
unresolved author leaves fromSelf absent, never false
referenced author id equal to the bot id is fromSelf true
ids differing only by case or padding are not fromSelf
Telegram from.id 0 is a real author id, not an unknown author
source assertion: one botUserId value and one resolve call feed both halves of Telegram's mentioned

contractCoverage.obligation: one compact header line, no JSON, always the referenced message id, clear ours marker, and user-controlled excerpt text can neither forge header structure nor emit a lone surrogate
cases: REGRESSION-2: a full forged segment attempt leaves exactly one [, one ], one quote pair, one author: and two msg: tokens
10 sanitiser bypass attempts (doubled brackets, look-alike brackets, fullwidth quotes, RTL override, zero-width in msg:/author:, uppercase MSG:, spaced mSg :) all keep the structural fingerprint
an excerpt that sanitises to blank renders no quoted section, not an empty pair
a hostile excerpt can neither remove the real id nor flip the ours marker
REGRESSION-1 / REGRESSION-3: code-point truncation at the adapter 200 and header 120 bounds emits no lone surrogate
astral point straddling the bound is dropped whole; chained adapter+header truncation leaves exactly one ellipsis
newlines, tabs and CR collapse so the header stays one line

residualFindings.finding: Unicode look-alike delimiters (U+FF3D, U+2769, U+FF02), RTL override U+202E and zero-width characters are not stripped, so a referenced message can render text that LOOKS like a second header segment.
residualFindings.whyAccepted: It cannot BE one: every ASCII delimiter of the header grammar stays unique and the text stays inside the quoted section. Stripping arbitrary look-alikes would mangle legitimate CJK punctuation.

contractCoverage.obligation: engagement policy untouched: a Discord reply never sets mentioned; Telegram's pre-existing reply-to-bot promotion is preserved
cases: Discord: mentioned is computed with no reply input (source assertion over adapter-discord/src/main.ts)
Telegram: mentioned still promotes a reply to the bot
Telegram: refactored mentioned matches the pre-change expression on realistic inputs
Telegram: the only divergences are unreachable payloads, enumerated below

enumeratedDivergences.after: fromSelf is absent, so mentioned is false

enumeratedDivergences.input: reply_to_message from the bot with no usable message_id
enumeratedDivergences.after: not a reply, so no promotion

deferred.reason: conversation_context (message_id, origin_key, author_id, author_name, body, received_at, consumed_at) has no column for it, and inbound_messages.engagement_json exists only for ENGAGED messages while the unread digest is mostly DECLINED messages, so a join would give partial silently-lossy coverage. The brief forbids a schema migration.
deferred.liveCoverage: the live header path IS durable: engagement_json is persisted before dispatch and re-read in runInboundTurn
